verdict.headline: Intel's worst day since 1974 drags chip stocks down and gives the Nasdaq its worst month in 19 months
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 -1.82% to 7,579.97, Nasdaq -2.86% to 25,437.00, Dow -1.1% to 51,770.31; Russell 2000 -1.7%; SOX about -7%; VIX 19.42; 10Y ~4.91%; Brent (Dec) $117.64; gold $3,898.90; BTC $77,173. Intel -28.58%; Nasdaq -5.3% for October.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: Intel fell 28.58% to $65.76, its worst day since 1974, after guiding fourth-quarter revenue to $15–$16 billion against $17.07 billion expected. The semiconductor index fell about 7% and chip stocks lost roughly $1 trillion. The Nasdaq fell 2.86% to 25,437.00, ending the week about 2% lower and October down 5.3%, its worst month since March 2025.

What it means: the selling moved from the companies buying AI hardware to the companies making it. Amazon recovered most of a 7% premarket loss and closed about 2% lower, while AMD fell 10.88% and Nvidia 4.22%. Intel's miss is mostly its own (PC demand, supply limits, an Israel plant explosion), but the market priced it across the sector. Bonds rallied and December hike odds fell to 72.7% from 83.0%, but Brent rose 2.4% to a six-month high, so lower yields came with a higher inflation risk.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close back above 25,955.34 would undo the week's decline. AMD's results on Tuesday are the first test of whether Intel's guide reads across to the rest of the sector, and a 10-year back above 5.11% before Friday's jobs report would mean oil had taken over from the demand for safety.
verdict.lede_short: Intel fell 28.58%, its worst day since 1974, and chip stocks fell about 7% with it, while Amazon recovered most of its premarket loss — the selling moved from AI's buyers to its suppliers. The Nasdaq fell 2.86%, ending October down 5.3%, its worst month since March 2025, as bonds rallied but oil hit a six-month high. A Nasdaq close back above 25,955.34 would undo the week; AMD's report on Tuesday tests whether Intel's miss spreads.

supporting_data.label: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15–$16 billion against $17.07 billion expected and EPS to $0.25 against $0.43, and fell 28.58% to $65.76 — supply limits and an Israel plant explosion drove a mostly company-specific miss that the market priced across the sector.
Chip stocks lost about $1 trillion as the semiconductor index fell about 7%, its second drop of more than 6% in just over a week — the selling has moved from AI's buyers to its suppliers.
The Nasdaq lost 5.3% in October, its worst month since March 2025, while the Dow rose 1.7% — the month's selling stayed concentrated in tech rather than spreading across stocks.

December hike odds on CME FedWatch fell to 72.7% from 83.0% and the 2-year fell about 10 bp to 4.585% — the market expects the tech selling to make the Fed somewhat less aggressive, even as Musalem said hikes may be needed soon.

Brent's December contract settled up 2.4% at $117.64 and WTI at $104.12, a six-month high, after more Hormuz tanker attacks — Brent gained 13.6% in October, the inflation input pushing against the bond rally.
Reddit fell 29.22% after guiding below consensus and blaming lower search referrals as Google expands AI Overviews — a measured cost of AI search to the sites that depend on Google traffic.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 4.22% to $204.64, less than half AMD's decline and well under the semiconductor index's ~7% drop.
Fell 10.88% to $504.80 ahead of its Tuesday report, the first chipmaker result after Intel's guide.
Recovered most of a 7% premarket loss to close about 2% lower despite negative $42.4 billion trailing free cash flow.
Fell 5.48% to $326.08 with the chip sector.
About $77,173 at 8:11pm ET, roughly flat over 24 hours after a $76,176 low, with $1.57 billion of liquidations after the Binance theft.

trade_setups.thesis: The semiconductor index has had two drops of more than 6% in just over a week after Intel's guide, with AMD down 10.88% into its Tuesday report.
trade_setups.entry: AMD $504.80 and Nvidia $204.64 closes; Nasdaq 25,437 below, 25,955.34 above.
trade_setups.invalidation: A steady AMD guide would make Intel's miss look company-specific; a Nasdaq close above 25,955.34 would undo the week's decline. A cautious AMD guide and a close under 25,437 would extend it.

trade_setups.thesis: The 10-year fell to about 4.91% on demand for safety while Brent rose 13.6% in October to a six-month high, so the two are pulling yields in opposite directions.
trade_setups.invalidation: A 10-year back above 5.11% before the jobs report would mean oil's inflation risk has taken over; December odds falling well below 70% would mean the safety bid is still winning.

trade_setups.thesis: BTC is holding about $1,000 above Friday's $76,176 low after the Binance theft and monthly options expiry, still below the $80,320 October 8 low.
trade_setups.invalidation: A daily close under $76,176 would extend the decline; a move back above $80,320 would make the theft a contained shock.
